title: Hooks reference
claims: PreToolUse receives tool parameters before processing, covers built-in and MCP tools, and can decide allow, deny, ask, or defer.
An Agent SDK callback hook that exceeds its timeout blocks the tool call.
notes: Product documentation; proprietary client/service, with no reusable implementation provenance.

title: Hook failure behavior
claims: Most hook failures or timeouts allow the triggering action unless a command or HTTP hook uses onFailure:block.
A policy hook with a wrong path can otherwise let the action continue.
notes: Follow-up to CW-01; documented integration condition, not a reproduced defect.

title: Configure permissions
claims: bypassPermissions skips permission prompts and is documented for isolated environments only.
Managed settings can disable bypassPermissions and auto mode.
notes: Second follow-up in the Claude supervision chain; describes current documented mitigation.

title: How Claude remembers your project
claims: Project instructions and auto memory are context rather than enforced configuration.
Startup loading is bounded and auto memory is machine-local.
notes: Separate memory boundary; no comparison runtime was exercised.

title: SDK child-process execution
claims: The SDK spawns the Codex executable and accepts thread, sandbox, approval, directory, cancellation, and environment options.
Without envOverride, the implementation copies the parent process environment into the child.
notes: Public repository source is Apache-2.0; source claim is unpinned main and requires an exact revision before reuse.

title: Sandbox approval logic
claims: Core source has policy-dependent approval requirements and rejects an escalation when required filesystem sandboxing is unavailable.
notes: Follow-up to CW-05; public source, unpinned main; hosted models/service are proprietary.

title: Windows sandbox setup issue #51777
claims: The issue was open when checked and reports Windows sandbox setup failure before browser or command execution.
The issue page showed no linked branch or pull request at the checked snapshot.
notes: Current open report, not reproduced here and not evidence of a general or unfixed Codex defect.

title: Permissions
claims: Permission rules resolve allow, ask, or deny by action, including tools, path-sensitive actions, subagents, and external directories.
Explicit denies remain enforced in auto mode, while most unspecified permissions default to allow.
notes: Current documentation; static permission behavior was not run locally.

title: Plugins
claims: Local project/global plugins and configured npm plugins are loaded at startup in documented order.
npm plugins and dependencies are installed automatically using Bun at startup.
notes: Follow-up to CW-08; current behavior is source/documentary only.

title: Dynamic plugin permission request issue #37164
claims: The issue was open when checked and states that tool.execute.before can inspect a call but cannot request the native once/always/reject permission UI after dynamic analysis.
The proposal states that explicit config deny rules should remain terminal and plugin-request failure should fall back to the normal prompt.
notes: Open enhancement request, not reproduced and not evidence that explicit deny is bypassable. Current source repository is MIT but needs a pinned release/commit and dependency inventory before reuse.

title: Pinned Pi coding-agent source and source audit
claims: Pinned Pi 1.4.0 is MIT, TypeScript/ESM, Node >=22.19.0, with source-observed hooks, nested dispatch, lifecycle, branch, MCP, and headless seams recorded in the local Pi source audit.
Extensions execute with Pi OS permissions and Pi transcript/session surfaces do not by themselves establish an independent durable effect ledger.
notes: Reuse provenance and detailed source claims are already recorded in pi-sources.json and pi-source-sources.json; no local install/runtime test.

title: Pinned Mnemopi package manifest and database source
claims: At the inspected OMP revision, Mnemopi declares Bun >=1.3.14 and its database source imports bun:sqlite.
The package is an OMP workspace component rather than a demonstrated Node-compatible Pi drop-in.
notes: Follow-up to CW-11; use only after pinning the OMP revision/license/dependency inventory and passing identical portability, export, deletion, and recovery gates.
